I'm scared of public speaking. So I decided to give a TEDx talk 🎤 My talk is about two things I believe deeply: prioritizing yourself first, and embracing your hardest moments. Through personal stories, I share how the hardest moments in life can become your greatest strengths, and how to put that mindset into practice every single day, starting from your own bed. A special shoutout to Anuj Patel, Alex Sriprathum, and the TEDxUCIrvine team for being there with me through every revision and rehearsal. Looking back, I realized my greatest memory wasn't executing the talk. It was the countless hours we spent bringing it to life. If you've got 10 minutes during lunch, I recommend giving it a watch. I'd love to hear what you think 😁 Link: https://lnkd.in/gTSVaibH

One post. 300K impressions. Two weeks ago, I committed to actually showing up consistently. I joined Intern Insider because I needed accountability to keep posting no matter what. I was overthinking my entire job search. My first week, I barely cracked 2K impressions. Now one post has crossed 300K. Momentum beats motivation. The biggest thing I've learned is that you don't need to feel ready to start. You just show up, stay consistent, and let momentum build. I'm only halfway through the fellowship and I'm just getting started. Super grateful for everyone who's supported me so far. If you're building your personal brand, recruiting for internships, or just trying to start posting, hmu. I'm down to figure it out together! Till next time 🫡

The only way to grow is by starting. From big tech internships to ambassadorships and fellowships, most of the opportunities that shaped me started with saying yes before I felt completely ready. Here's what starting actually looks like. 3 things you can do today: 1. Make a list of the opportunities you actually want and their deadlines It’s a lot easier to apply early when you already know what’s out there and when everything is due. 2. Update your resume now Not the night before an application is due. Do it while nothing is urgent. 3. Message one person doing exactly what you want to do Ask thoughtful questions, listen to their advice, and thank them for their time. Most of my opportunities came from having Intern Insider alerts on and applying the same day. The rest was just saying yes before I felt ready. If there’s one thing I could tell my younger self, it’s that you don’t need to have it all figured out. You just need to start.

I made a new project! It's called Perch and it's a desktop focus companion app where you can create a custom pixel-art mascot from any pictures you want (people, dogs, cats, etc.), and that mascot will sit in the corner of your desktop and reacts when you drift from the work you're meant to do. Built with Electron, React, TypeScript, SQLite, Codex, GPT-5.6, Nano Banana Pro (for mascot generation), and an optional Chrome MV3 Extension to see the chrome tabs you're on. I wanted to build a productivity app that also had some levels of emotional/mental connection and it makes focus support feel more personal, playful, and less judgemental. Github repo: https://lnkd.in/euMJ4b46 Had a lot of fun building this, especially as this was my first real desktop app and not just a web app. Love to hear what mascot you would make for your own focus companion :)
